A caller who already has tokenBalance of 1 should be allowed to call airDrop in the reference (balance unchanged), but the buggy version's hasNoBalance modifier requires balance == 1, so airDrop reverts for that caller.

When msg.sender calls airDrop() for the first time, the reference version succeeds and balance becomes 20, but the buggy version's hasNoBalance modifier requires balance == 1, causing the call to revert; the test asserts the call succeeds (not reverted).

When msg.sender calls airDrop() from the Bank contract, the reference contract accepts the call and increments tokenBalance, whereas the buggy version reverts because its supportsToken modifier checks 'Old Token' instead of 'Nu Token', causing the assertion of successful call to fail.
Alice calls airDrop() via a Bank whose supportsToken returns keccak256('Nu Token'); reference succeeds (tokenBalance becomes 20) while bug fails (require false).
